[b]Shutdown.[/b]

[i]"Not to be the bearer of bad news, but the diplomatic office has stood empty for a while now." The secretary, fidgeting, said to break the silence, hoping to avoid the ire of the military's supreme commander. And with a sigh, the supreme commander responded, "I am well aware..." She'd lean back in her chair and rest her hand on her forehead. "One headache after another, if it isn't the economy, then it's the north." With a pained sigh, she'd reach for a drawer, rummage through it before slamming it shut, causing the poor secretary to jump. "Bring me a glass of water and some painkillers. And don't bring me any more reports, I need time off from this trainwreck." 

The secretary nodded, but before she could leave, the supreme commander said, "Shut the diplomatic office down; they never answered to our request, and the north is too far up their own asses to even consider diplomacy." She'd nod, and then ask, "What about the corpora-" The supreme commander simply shook her head and slumped further in her chair, obviously too tired to continue this discussion.[/i]

[quote=qartena_hadasht;61000389]Upon deboarding the plane, he would see the beauty of Qartena Hadasht, and a warm wind would blow through his hair as he looked out over the tarmac. He was greeted by the Adir of Foreign Affairs Karam Eshmun and soldiers of the Sacred Band of Qartena Hadasht. The soldiers of the Sacred Band are wearing their ceremonial uniform, but are armed with their standard weapons. They perform a high step and salute upon him reaching the bottom of the stairs of the aircraft. Karam steps forward with an interpreter, he speaks. [i]"Greetings honored one, my name is Karam Eshmun and I am the Adir of Foreign Affairs. Thank you for coming to our great nation. If you follow me, I will lead you to our car so that we may go back to my office to begin our discussions."[/i] Karam would lead him back to a limousine that displayed two small flags of Qartena Hadasht above the headlights. A Soldier opened the door for the men and Karam would let Irman enter first. The soldier would close the door once both men were inside the vehicle, and they would begin their drive over to the Government sector.  [/quote]
Irman entered the car, thanking Karam. When he got comfortable, he took a moment to look around the limousine. He adjusted his fez. He would then turn to Karam, [i]"It is a great pleasure to speak with you. I hope that our talks will prove fruitful. There is more riding on this than you think."[/i] Irman tugged at his collar; it was uncomfortable, even more so now that he sat in a foreign car speaking with foreign men to an interpreter who may mistranslate and ruin his chances at being eternally enshrined into the history of the truest believers. He waited for Karam's reply, though the moments between the words leaving his lips and the time it took for the Adir to reply mounted his worry.
